performance.title: AI model performance
performance.description: Understand AI model latency, throughput, reliability, and the trade-offs that shape real product performance.
performance.heroDescription: Model performance is the shape of an experience: when an answer starts, how smoothly it arrives, and whether the system stays dependable under load.
performance.askStart: How quickly does useful work begin?
performance.askResult: How fast does the result arrive?
performance.askSuccess: How often does the path succeed?
performance.measuresDescription: Treating these as one score makes model selection simpler—and usually wrong.
performance.timeToFirstTokenDescription: How long someone waits before the response begins. This is the metric users feel first.
performance.timeToFirstTokenGoodFor: Chat, copilots, voice and interactive agents
performance.outputSpeedDescription: How quickly text arrives after generation starts. It determines whether a long answer feels fluid or laboured.
performance.outputSpeedGoodFor: Long-form generation, coding and batch workloads
performance.endToEndLatencyDescription: The complete request journey, including routing, provider queues, inference and network transfer.
performance.endToEndLatencyGoodFor: Tools, structured outputs and multi-step workflows
performance.watchDescription: The same response streams below at three different relative speeds. Compare the pause before generation with the pace after the first token arrives.
performance.experienceTitle: The best model depends on the experience
performance.experienceDescription: Illustrative profiles show why a single leaderboard cannot describe every product. Shorter latency bars are better; longer throughput and reliability bars are better.
performance.tradeoffsNote: These profiles explain trade-offs; they are not live measurements or model rankings.
performance.waitDescription: Total latency is a chain, not a single model measurement. Breaking the request into stages shows where optimisation will actually help.
performance.longestStageDescription: Faster routing cannot compensate for a long provider queue. A faster model cannot fix repeated tool calls.
performance.uptimeDescription: Availability percentages are easier to reason about when translated into the interruption they allow.
performance.constraintDescription: Performance work becomes clearer when the user experience—not an abstract score—sets the target.
performance.conversationalDetail: A fast start usually matters more than peak output speed. Stream early and keep the response moving.
performance.longAnswersDetail: Measure generation separately so provider queues do not hide a slow model behind one average.
performance.toolsDetail: The model can be fast while orchestration is slow. Track routing, retries and tool calls separately.
performance.frameworkDescription: Compare real models across benchmarks, pricing and Phaseo Gateway performance signals.
